summary.text: Radiometric dating finds the age of materials such as rocks by comparing a natural radioactive isotope with the decay products it forms at a known constant rate.
Pioneered by Ernest Rutherford and Bertram Boltwood in 1906 and 1907, it is now the main source of absolute ages for rocks, fossils and Earth itself.

facts.label: Half-lives used
facts.value: About 10 years to over 100 billion years

items.prompt: A rock sample is put under great heat and pressure in a lab. What happens to the decay rate of most radioactive atoms in it?

options.label: It speeds up sharply
It slows almost to a stop
It stays essentially the same
It reverses for a short time

items.explain: For most nuclides the half-life depends only on nuclear properties and is not affected by temperature, pressure or chemical environment.

items.prompt: You watch a single unstable atom. Can you say when it will decay?

options.label: Yes, at exactly one half-life
No, though a large group decays predictably
Yes, if you know its temperature
No, and large groups are random too

items.explain: The moment a particular nucleus decays is unpredictable, but a collection of such atoms decays exponentially at a rate set by the half-life.

items.prompt: For a rock's measured age to be trustworthy with the basic equation, what must be true since the rock formed?

options.label: It must have stayed below freezing
It must have lain flat and untilted
It must hold fossils of known age
No parent or daughter atoms came or went

items.explain: The basic equation requires that neither the parent nuclide nor the daughter product entered or left the material after its formation.

items.prompt: An unstable atom decays through a chain of short-lived steps before becoming stable. Which half-life usually matters most for dating?

options.label: The longest one in the chain
The shortest one in the chain
The very first step's only
The average of all the steps

items.explain: In a decay chain the half-life of interest is usually the longest one, since it limits the rate of the whole transformation to the stable daughter.

items.prompt: Two different radiometric methods are used on the same ancient rock. Why might a lab bother with both?

options.label: Each method only works on half the rock
Matching results help confirm the age
Averaging two wrong ages makes a right one
One method is needed to switch the other on

items.explain: Correlation between methods can confirm an age; Greenland's Amitsoq gneisses gave consistent ages by uranium–lead and lead–lead dating.

items.prompt: Besides dating rocks on Earth, what else is radiometric dating used to investigate?

options.label: The age of light from distant stars
The speed of today's ocean currents
The origins of meteorites and asteroids
The future dates of volcanic eruptions

items.explain: Radiometric dating is also used to investigate the origins of meteorites and asteroids.
